title: fix: keep chat usable after removing an unavailable tool server
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/issues/1717

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes later chat turns failing after an unavailable stdio tool server is removed on POSIX process-group runtimes.

## User Impact

Users can remove a server whose executable cannot start and continue the same conversation. The original launch error and retry diagnostic remain visible.

## Why This Change Was Made

Failed command startup never sends `ready`, so the cleanup owner lost the process-group anchor identity. Include that identity in the failure receipt and join bounded, authoritative cleanup before returning the launch error. Receipt, lineage, relay-exit, and kernel extinction checks remain required; genuine cleanup failures still reject.

## Evidence

Regression negative controls on base `8197f6f8cf4` failed for missing anchor identity, premature failed-start readiness, and same-session removal (`cleanup could not confirm closure`). The production owner files in the rebased parent are unchanged from that baseline. With this fix, the real-process session regression removes the unavailable server and prepares the next turn successfully.

## Required proof pools

Gateway-only change. Windows integration evidence covers `windows-11-arm64` and `windows-winui-interactive` from the [Companion proof pools](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw-windows-node/blob/main/docs/PROOF_POOLS.md). The real Gateway path was exercised on Linux with Bun; `windows-wsl-gateway-e2e` is not qualified by this proof.

## Validation

Final source tree at `b882bbf627b410599fe231e2a917b4d6a80e76d3`:

- `pnpm build:runtime`: passed, 45.9s.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with the nine affected lifecycle test files: **97 passed, 2 Windows-only skipped**, 44.61s.
- `pnpm build:plugin-sdk:dts` and canonical `scripts/package-openclaw-for-docker.mjs --allow-unreleased-changelog --skip-build`: passed. The package identifies the exact final commit and passed inventory/import integrity validation.
- Core type check, six-file type-aware lint, formatting, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent code review, structured review, and final commit-coherence review: clean. The final amendment only corrected committer metadata; its source tree is identical to the reviewed and tested tree.
- The optional repository-wide changed check flags an inherited max-lines suppression in `src/commands/doctor-database-port.ts`. That file and its baseline are byte-identical to the PR parent, outside this fix. Additional broad test type graphs are covered by PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

[Final-head live proof, correlated Gateway diagnostic, and screenshot](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171397#issuecomment-6157181345).

The test used actual Store Companion `2026.9.803.0`, Windows 11 ARM64, local `qwen3.6-35b-a3b-mtp-ud-q4-k-s` (32,768 context), and an isolated Linux Gateway on official Bun `1.4.3`. Configuration: `tools.profile=minimal`, `tools.alsoAllow=["bundle-mcp"]`; stdio server `blender-mcp`, command `/mnt/c/openclaw-issue-1717-missing/uvx.exe`, argument `blender-mcp`. Live changes used `config.get` / `config.patch` with revision and destructive-array acknowledgements.

The supported package updater transitioned official stable `2026.10.3` (`59cb44796b0f`) to the exact validated candidate (also manifest `2026.10.3`) and reported `status: ok`. Settings, workspace, model, tools, the Companion Gateway record, stored device credential, and conversation survived. The old host exited cleanly on replaced installation identity; the candidate was then activated. No older-host recovery or mixed-version host retention is claimed.

The activated candidate retained its Gateway PID through real stdio worker replacement, discovery, invocation, removal, and confirmed closure. In the same conversation, missing-executable startup then produced ENOENT/unavailable diagnostics; removal succeeded without restart, and `UPGRADE_RECOVERY_1717` plus `UPGRADE_FOLLOWUP_1717` completed while **Connected**. Neither cleanup warning appeared.

![Final-head Companion remains Connected and completes recovery and follow-up after unavailable-server removal](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d177a783-8bbc-4a18-b9f6-50e4d3448c7a)

**Not verified:** WSL packaging, the original installer readiness contradiction, and the originally reported repeated restart loop. This PR addresses the reproduced cleanup follow-on failure; the broader related issue remains open. Bun exercises the repaired POSIX owner; existing native Node/Linux cleanup repairs are prior work.
